memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Rebekah was told what her older son Esau had said, she sent for her younger son Jacob and said to him, 'Your brother Esau is planning to avenge himself by killing you. Now then, my son, do what I say: Flee at once to my brother Laban in Harran. Stay with him for a while until your brother's fury subsides. When your brother is no longer angry with you and forgets what you did to him, I'll send word for you to come back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?'" - Gen 27:42-45 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the scheme's bitter harvest comes in. Rebekah, who had engineered the whole deception, must send her beloved Jacob far away to save his life. She says, "Stay with him for a while" — but that "while" would stretch into twenty long years. The heartbreaking truth is that Rebekah, as far as Scripture records, never saw her favourite son again.

Here we see a solemn law of life: "A man reaps what he sows" (Gal 6:7). Rebekah sowed deception to gain the blessing, and she reaped the loss of the very son she loved. Jacob, too, would reap what he sowed — the deceiver would himself be deceived by Laban, and later by his own sons. Sin's consequences boomerang in ways we never expect.

This is not said to crush us, but to sober us. Our choices carry real weight; they ripple into our families and our futures. The pain in this family was self-inflicted, born of grasping instead of trusting God.

Yet even here, grace is hidden. God would use these twenty years away to humble and shape Jacob into a new man. Our God is able to redeem even the messes we make, working them for good as we return to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might I be sowing something I will not want to reap?
2. Do I see how my choices ripple into those I love?
3. Can I trust God to redeem even the consequences of my mistakes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to sow wisely, in trust rather than in scheming. And where I face the harvest of past mistakes, redeem it by Your grace and shape me through it. Amen.
